title: Protoplasm behaves as a highly viscous fluid that changes shape under force

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Protoplasm behaves as a highly viscous fluid that changes shape under force

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The protoplasm of an Amoeba deforms and flows under the slightest pressure, so it is a fluid, but it is far more viscous than water, like treacle, and this viscosity slows its changes of shape.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: While the protoplasm of the Amoeba reacts to the slightest pressure, and tends to “flow,” and while we therefore speak of it as a fluid, it is evidently far less mobile than such a fluid, for instance, as water, but is rather like treacle in its slow creeping movements as it changes its shape in response to force.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter I, “Introductory”; topic “Physical properties of the Amoeba”. Scope: protoplasm of Amoeba and similar naked cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch01-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The phenomenology maps well to standard rheological measurements, giving good operationalizability and discrimination. Existing public data are mostly imaging rather than complete force-response experiments, so only a restricted test is currently practical.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate effective viscosity and viscoelastic relaxation from time-resolved amoeba deformation under known pressure or force, and compare flow and relaxation with water and high-viscosity reference fluids. Slow force-dependent flow with a much larger effective viscosity would support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public images seldom include calibrated applied pressure.

Protoplasm is active and viscoelastic, not a passive Newtonian fluid.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.35
analysis feasibility: 0.6
discriminating power: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.85
data existence: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Viscosity, yield under slight pressure, and the timescale of shape change are standard variables, so the contrast with water and with an elastic solid is a real decision criterion. The measurements exist but are scattered across microrheology papers, cover a modest set of naked cells, and do not by themselves separate passive treacle-like viscosity from active flow. Compilation and that confound make the test partial rather than immediate.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare cytoplasmic viscosity and creep of Amoeba, or closely similar naked cells, with water under small stress, and compare the flow timescale with the timescale of shape change. The claim is confirmed by ready flow, viscosity orders of magnitude above water, and a slowing of shape change by that viscosity; it is refuted if the material is elastic on that timescale or near water in viscosity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Active cytoskeletal flow can imitate high passive viscosity.

Viscosities differ by method and are not gathered in one downloadable rheology table.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.45
data existence: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.45
